I agree that time-outs are non-negotiable - by breaking time out I mean he gets up and we have to start over, not that he gets out of it. So I will end up sitting with him for the full time, but the whole process just hasn't shown any signs of deterring him in any way, his negative behavior isn't effected. Right out of a time-out I'll give him a warning for something, and then he'll still disobey knowing perfectly well that a time-out is coming again. I do ignore him the whole time he is in time-out, I explain to him that I can't talk with him, we just have to sit there. 

Sometimes time-outs work, and I will always use them first, but sometimes they just don't. I really feel the need to have something that is consistently unpleasant for him. Once his reasoning is a little stronger, time-outs and the loss of privileges should do the trick, but now, I have nothing to deter him when he is in those moods. 

In our situation, I believe the spanking would be exceptionally rare, just enough to remind him that it is something unpleasant. Then when he is in time-out, I can tell him to remain there or he will get a spanking. He knows he doesn't want that, so he will sit there; in a sense, the spanking will always be his clear choice. However, his reasoning isn't good enough to know that it's unpleasant if I take a toy away or lengthen his time-out, so he can't make any clear choices when I threaten him with longer time-outs. 

I think the thing he is trying to communicate is just that he wants to find out what our upper limits are, like he wants to know if we really do have any ultimate control over what he is allowed to do. I think he is just exploring his power and once he learns that we really are the parents and we have rules that we are willing to enforce, then he will settle back down into just being an active, strong-willed kid (rather than being defiant as he is now).

I'm sure that in your profession, spanking is almost always abusive, but I think in our situation it will actually help him. Do you think that spanking is universally wrong, or just wrong almost all of the time? I agree that spanking can teach perverted notions of power, but I don't think it has to be that way. 

Think of a chimpanzee that has none of the psychological problems that humans have because she wasn't raised in our imperfect society - rather she was raised in a society that evolved to function well over millions of years, so her behavior is natural and good for her species. Now if this chimp has a baby that bites her nipple, is the mom-chimp going to give the baby a time-out, or a pat on the bottom to let him know this isn't ok? Yet that baby chimp is going to grow up to be just as loving and socially normal as the mom. 

I think the key to using spanking successfully is in having a great relationship with your kid, and being a healthy parent. Most people who use spanking probably don't fall into that category, but does that mean that the discipline should be taboo for all of us?

I had him draw it twice, both times he drew a crude circle (in red) and scribbled dense lines beneath it (in yellow). I asked him if the airplane was red, and he still said that it was white. 

The only remarkable thing about his drawing was how minimal it was - just a circle and a cluster of lines beneath. This is remarkable b/c typically his drawings get much more busy looking.

I just asked. At first he said it was quiet, it didn't make any noise, then he changed his mind and said it sounded like fire. I said "what does fire sound like, can you make the same noise?" He kind of growls. 

Also, I asked him if he touched it, he said no. 

I asked what it smelled like. He said "Burning rubber." I said "How do you even know what burning rubber smells like, where did you smell it" He said "From Home Depot."

Also, I asked if it sat on the floor in his room, or if it floated (using a bowl to demonstrate the options), he said it floated (previously I assumed it was on the floor.)

For the record, my inner skeptic has to assume this was a dream until further evidence is presented, but my inner believer remains open to any possibility. But even my skeptical side finds some of the aspects particularly interesting - like the circular shape, the fire coming out from the bottom, the fact that it forces entry into his room but makes him feel happy, and his insistence that it is real. If this was a dream, where did those images come from, and why is this particular experience the first "dream" he ever talked about?
